subject.title: [Bug]: Kimi Coding auth fallback in systemd Gateway when config env is not injected

question: For managed systemd Gateways, should provider API keys from the config `env` block be a supported runtime credential source, or should daemon users be steered to `.env`, SecretRef, or per-agent auth profiles instead?
rationale: Both options affect credential persistence and status semantics; automation should not choose whether OpenClaw should materialize config secrets into supervisor env files or change the documented Kimi setup path.

options.title: Support config env in daemons
options.body: Keep the documented Kimi config path supported and add focused service-env/runtime/status tests plus live proof that systemd Gateway turns use it consistently.

options.title: Make daemon auth profile or dotenv only
options.body: Update docs and `models status` so config-env credentials are not presented as effective daemon runtime auth unless they are in `.env`, SecretRef, or the per-agent auth store.

options.title: Fold into broader env unification
options.body: Defer this specific Kimi/systemd case to the broader env-source precedence issue, accepting that this report remains unresolved until that contract lands.

recommendation.title: Support config env in daemons
recommendation.body: Keep the documented Kimi config path supported and add focused service-env/runtime/status tests plus live proof that systemd Gateway turns use it consistently.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision primarily sits on managed-service env behavior and config/auth compatibility, where Vincent has adjacent ownership signals and co-author history.
